content_preview.summary: The FCC blocked new imports of foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots and power inverters, a move aimed at China, which ships more than 85% of the world's humanoid robots.

editor_notes.originality: REJECT basis, decided on the merits against the actual content of the published article. This is the THIRD submission on the identical July 28, 2026 FCC Covered List action targeting foreign-made humanoid/quadruped robots and power inverters. Article #1 (src/content/articles/2026-07/30-fcc-bans-new-chinese-made-humanoid-robots-and-robot-dogs-citing-national-security-risks.md) was already published from PR #2081, covering: the FCC order, the 'advanced robotic devices' definition, the same 85% China market-share figure, the same 15,000-units/5,000+-Unitree-AGIBOT/few-hundred-Tesla-Figure-AI shipment breakdown, the same Carr 'secure America's critical supply chains' quote, the same 'networked capabilities... vectors for attacks' FCC quote, the same prospective-only/no-recall framing, the same Conditional Approval (DoW/DHS) process, the same Mao Ning quote, the same September Trump-Xi meeting framing, and an Analysis section making essentially the same 'targeted supply-chain move, not a market-wide recall' point this submission's Analysis makes. Submission #2 (PR #2084) covering the same event was already REJECTED for exactly this reason, despite containing incremental details the published article lacked (Route Fifty's Huawei/ZTE historical-precedent framing, the Pentagon's Unitree military-ties listing, CGTN as a direct China-state-media citation) — the reviewer at the time correctly judged those incremental facts as 'supplementary color on the same event, not a materially different angle.' This submission (#3) is, on the merits, WEAKER on originality than #2: it shares 3 of its 5 sources verbatim with the already-published article (CBS News, Fortune, Robotics and Automation News), cites a different FCC document number (DOC-423682A1, a fact sheet, vs. the published article's DA-26-786A1 order) for the same underlying action rather than new information, and its one genuinely new source (Forbes) contains material the article does not actually use — Forbes reports a granular 10-company shipment breakdown (Agibot 5,168 / Unitree 4,200 / UBTech 1,000 / etc.), a $150B in US robotics venture funding, and Unitree's July 22 commercial launch in Europe, none of which appear anywhere in this submission's body_markdown. The submission's Analysis section — that the Covered List mechanism was 'previously used against foreign telecommunications equipment' — is a vaguer, unsourced-by-name echo of the same historical-precedent point Route Fifty made with specifics (Huawei/ZTE) in the already-rejected #2, not new ground. A reader who saw the published article gains no meaningfully new fact, quote, or angle from this submission. Per Step 5 of the review process, this is 'the exact same story already published' with 'no new information or angle' — REJECT, consistent with the #2084 precedent and, if anything, an easier call given this submission's thinner differentiation.
